step_by_step_reasoning: The whiteboard depicts a batch processing and monitoring architecture on AWS. At the top center is an S3 icon labeled 'DATALAKE'. Below it are 'EC2', 'BATCH', and 'FSx' (FSX). EC2 and BATCH are circled together. An arrow points from BATCH to FSx. From FSx, an arrow labeled 'DRT' (Data Repository Task) points up to DATALAKE (S3). From the BATCH circle, an arrow labeled 'Events' points down to EVENTBRIDGE. From EVENTBRIDGE, an arrow points right to LAMBDA. Between LAMBDA and ELASTICSEARCH (OpenSearch), there are two arrows in opposite directions (one pointing right, one pointing left).

graph.name: Biopharma MRI Data Processing Pipeline
graph.categories: Batch Processing, Data Analytics, Healthcare & Life Sciences
graph.notes: The architecture processes MRI data using AWS Batch, FSx for Lustre, S3 Data Lake, EventBridge, Lambda, and Elasticsearch (OpenSearch).

nodes.name: DATALAKE
nodes.notes: Stores input MRI data and receives processed results via Data Repository Tasks (DRT)

nodes.name: EC2
nodes.notes: Compute instances launched and managed by AWS Batch

nodes.name: BATCH
nodes.notes: Orchestrates batch jobs across EC2 instances

nodes.name: FSx
nodes.notes: High-performance storage mounted to EC2 instances

nodes.name: EVENTBRIDGE
nodes.notes: Captures job status events from AWS Batch

nodes.name: LAMBDA
nodes.notes: Processes job events and logs for indexing

nodes.name: ELASTICSEARCH
nodes.notes: Indexes events and logs for monitoring and Kibana visualization

edges.notes: FSx syncs results back to S3 Data Lake via Data Repository Task (DRT)
Batch sends job status events to EventBridge
Lambda indexes events and logs into Elasticsearch
Elasticsearch queries / status checks returned to Lambda
